newsitem.title: USA: US rate rise would hike Argentine rates -Fernandez.
newsitem.headline: US rate rise would hike Argentine rates -Fernandez.

text.p: Higher U.S. interest rates would have an immediate and significant impact on Argentina's domestic dollar and peso debt, said Roque Fernandez, Finance Minister of Argentina.

In a press briefing in New York on Friday after a conference organized by Price Waterhouse, Fernandez said a rise in U.S. interest rates would produce an immediate increase in interest rates in Argentina.
"Argentina domestic interest rates and U.S. interest rate denominated in pesos .. are very significantly affected by the U.S. interest rate policy plus country risk," he said.
Without restrictions on capital flows, interest rate arbitrage would transmit the higher U.S. rate immediately to Argentina, he said.
"That's exactly the arbitrage that we set up for the equilibrium in the Argentina domestic market and the international market," he said.

Noting that the peso rate spread is related to expectations for Argentina's exchange rate policy, Fernandez said: "We believe the increase in the U.S. interest rate will also increase the peso interest rate."

Brazil's Finance Minister Pedro Malan, who was also at the press briefing, avoided a direct comment on the impact of higher U.S. rates on Brazil, saying that whether the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise rates and how the market would react remains a conjecture at this point.
